newsitem.title: KENYA: UN Rwanda trial suspended until March.
newsitem.headline: UN Rwanda trial suspended until March.

text.p: The U.N. tribunal on Rwanda has suspended for two weeks the trial of a former mayor accused of participating in the 1994 genocide of an estimated 800,000 people, a tribunal spokesman said on Monday.
"The trial of Jean-Paul Akayesu is suspended until March 6 and then they will carry on with prosecution witnesses," said tribunal spokesman Bocar Sy.
No official reason was given for the suspension but the trial's three judges were due to attend a conference in Cape Town, South Africa, Sy said.
Akayesu, 43, is the first suspect to be tried before the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, set up in November 1994 to bring to justice the main architects of the Rwandan genocide.

Since the trial began on January 9 prosecution witnesses have testified that Akayesu ordered and participated directly in killings of Tutsis and political enemies in Taba commune, south Rwanda, where he was mayor.
The trial of Georges Rutaganda, vice-president of the extremist Interahamwe militia, has been delayed until March 11, Sy said.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan met three senior tribunal officials on Friday after an internal U.N. report earlier this month accused the tribunal of inefficiency and waste, mismanagement and corruption.
